title: Topological inverse system of punctured compact open neighborhoods
statement: Let $T$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space], $Z\subseteq T$ closed. Put $I=(\operatorname{compactOpenNeighborhoods}(Z))^{\mathrm{op}}$, ordered by reverse inclusion, using [def-weil-pbc-punctured-neighborhood-cohomology-diagram]. Define $S_i=N_i\setminus Z$ with its subspace topology, transition maps $f_{ij}:S_j\hookrightarrow S_i$, and projections $p_i:S\hookrightarrow S_i$ from $S=\{t:(\overline{\{t\}}\cap Z)\ne\varnothing,\ t\notin Z\}$. Then $I$ is nonempty and directed. If $Z^c$ is compact, all $S_i$ are spectral and all $f_{ij}$ are spectral maps. Compatible tuples in the $S_i$ have exactly one preimage in $S$, and the topology of $S$ is $\inf_i p_i^*\tau_{S_i}$. Under the same compact-complement hypothesis the punctured generalization subspace itself is spectral.

proof.text: The whole ambient space is an index; intersection of two indices is a common later index, compact by quasi-separatedness.

The punctures are compact opens by quasi-separatedness. Mathlib Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.spectralSpace gives spectrality of each subspace. For a compact open V of a stage, its ambient image is compact open; its intersection with the later puncture is compact by quasi-separatedness, and embedding reflection of compactness proves the transition is spectral.

If the closure of a point misses Z, use the compact-open basis to cover Z inside the complement of that closure. Compactness of the closed subset Z gives a finite subcover; its union is an index missing the point. Thus the intersection of all indices is exactly the generalizations of Z, including when Z is empty.

Compare each tuple coordinate to the whole-space index. Their ambient values are equal; that value lies in every index and outside Z, so the preceding characterization constructs the unique point of S. All projections are continuous, and the whole-space coordinate induces exactly the subspace topology. These two observations give both topology inequalities.
Apply the spectral directed inverse-limit theorem to this concrete system and its just proved topological limit, obtaining spectrality of the punctured generalization subspace.

lean.statement: theorem puncturedNeighborhood_topologicalLimit {T : Type u} [TopologicalSpace T] [SpectralSpace T] (Z : Set T) (hZ : IsClosed Z) : (∀ a : ∀ i : puncturedNeighborhoodIndex Z, puncturedNeighborhoodSpace Z hZ i, (∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), puncturedNeighborhoodTransition Z hZ i j h (a j) = a i) → ∃! x : puncturedGeneralizations Z, ∀ i, puncturedNeighborhoodProjection Z hZ i x = a i) ∧ (TopCat.of (puncturedGeneralizations Z)).str = ⨅ i : puncturedNeighborhoodIndex Z, TopologicalSpace.induced (puncturedNeighborhoodProjection Z hZ i) (puncturedNeighborhoodSpace Z hZ i).str
